newsitem.title: UK: Tesco in 630 mln stg Irish shopping spree.
newsitem.headline: Tesco in 630 mln stg Irish shopping spree.

text.p: British supermarket chain Tesco Plc said on Friday it had agreed to buy Associated British Food Plc's food retailing and related businesses in Ireland for 630 million pounds ($1 billion).

Tesco said it was buying 75 Quinnsworth and Crazy Prices stores in the Republic of Ireland and 34 stores in Northern Ireland trading as Stewarts, Crazy Prices, Superdeal, Westside Stores and Bloomfield.

Tesco said in a statement that ABF would also receive a 10 million pound ($15.9 million) dividend before completion and that excluding rationalisation and integration costs, the acquisition was expected to cover financing costs in the first year, "with further benefits accruing thereafter."
Tesco said that included in the deal were processing and packaging businesses and Wine Barrel, an off licence chain, along with Lifestyle Sports and Leisure sports shops.

"This is a strong and successful business with a proven management and we look to add to that with our own strengths and to continue the success achieved so far," Tesco, Britain's biggest supermarket group, said.

The deal has been on the cards for several days and Tesco said on Thursday that talks with ABF were continuing after the Financial Times newspaper reported that they had broken down. Privately-owned Irish supermarket group Superquinn has said it might consider a bid for ABF's stores. ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
